translation.english_title: Ammaiyappa, grant your grace — all is your doing

english_lines: Ammaiyappa, grant your grace — all is your doing,
Ammaiyappa,
All is your doing, Ammaiyappa.
notes: `அம்மையப்பா` is retained as `Ammaiyappa` rather than reduced to a generic `Lord`, because the name/vocative is central to the lyric and film title.

english_lines: Ammaiyappa, grant your grace — all is your doing,
Ammaiyappa,
All is your doing, Ammaiyappa.
notes: The full opening is repeated because the source repeats it after the performance label; it is not collapsed into a refrain reference.

english_lines: This life, the afterlife; pleasure, pain,
Truth, falsehood, the bonds of the world —
All is your doing, Ammaiyappa.
notes: The paired opposites are preserved as an accumulation rather than rewritten into explanatory prose.

source_tamil_lines: அரசன் முதல் ஆண்டிகளும் ஐயன் சிருஷ்டி உண்மையப்பா
english_lines: Poison in honey, clear nectar, honey-cascade, fire-forest,
Burning pool, volcanoes — all are your doing, Ammaiyappa;
From the king down to aandis, all are Aiyan's creation — true, appa,
This is Aiyan's creation — true, appa.
notes: The source's rapid paradoxical image-chain — honey/poison, nectar, honey-cascade, fire-forest, burning pool, volcanoes — remains concrete.
`ஆண்டிகள்` is retained as `aandis` because a simple `beggars` or `ascetics` would over-fix the social/religious register; the contrast with `அரசன்` is preserved.
`ஐயன்` and the vocative `அப்பா` remain audible as `Aiyan` and `appa` rather than being normalized into a single English divine title.

source_tamil_lines: பல்லக்கு தூக்கிகளும் அதில் பவனி வருகின்ற மனிதர்களும்
english_lines: The palanquin-bearers, and the people who ride in procession within it,
Ammaiyappa — within your
Bounds they live; that is true, appa,
The toad within the stone, the oil within sesame,
The cruel venom within the snake's fang —
Ammaiyappa, this ancient world says
That all of it is your doing, appa.
notes: The bearers/riders contrast is kept visible; the lyric does not flatten social hierarchy into a generic statement that `everyone is equal`.
`கல்லுக்குள் தேரை` is rendered as the traditional image of a toad within stone; `எள்ளுக்குள் எண்ணெய்` and snake-fang venom remain equally concrete.
The source line-break after `உந்தன்` is preserved in the mapping rather than hidden by a prose rewrite.

translator_notes: This song combines devotional address, paradox, social hierarchy and proverbial natural images. The translation keeps those registers together rather than turning it into generalized piety.
No singer is inferred because the verified Tamil record says the numbered lyric page prints no separate voice line.
This is a literary source-faithful translation, not a singable adaptation.
